newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's 1997 GDP seen rising 6.4 pct - KDI.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's 1997 GDP seen rising 6.4 pct - KDI.

text.p: South Korea's gross domestic product (GDP) is expected to grow a real 6.4 percent in 1997 against this year's estimated growth of 7.0 percent, the Korea Development Institute said on Thursday.

The government's leading economic think-tank said GDP growth would slow to 6.1 percent in the first half of 1997, mainly due to falling export prices, but pick up in the second half when growth would reach 6.7 percent.
A statement said the consumer price index, South Korea's leading inflation indicator, would gain 4.7 percent in 1997, against an estimated 4.5 percent this year.
Wage rises and the Korean won's depreciation against the dollar would fuel inflation early next year, it said.
The institute also forecast the nation's current account deficit at about $15.5 billion next year, down from an estimated $21.9 billion for this year.
The larger deficit this year was mainly because of the fall in prices for South Korea's leading exports, including computer chips, petrochemicals and steel.
